patterns.purpose: Show the product idea in one glance and get a business owner to request a walkthrough.
sections: Light header with Request a walkthrough
Hero promise beside a coded mini dashboard and one small photo tile
The problem: three sources converging into one tile
Benefits bento where each tile answers one question
Drill-down proof: linked cards with coded previews of the calendar, table, and board
Roles teaser with a wide team banner
patterns.desktop: 12-column grid inside 80rem. Primary tiles span 6–8 columns, secondary 4, compact 3. Photos sit inside tiles at card radius. Benefits: Today 7, Bookings 5, Follow-ups 4, Team 4, Performance 4.
patterns.mobile: One column in DOM order, which is the reading order. The coded dashboard stays before supporting photos; the CTA image moves below its copy and swaps to the 4:5 crop.
patterns.conversion: Request a walkthrough stays in the header and CTA band. See a sample dashboard is the secondary path into the portal.

patterns.purpose: Prove the bento works as a useful daily overview in which every tile leads to a full view.
sections: Today tile with the next three visits
Confirmation tile in the warning state
Follow-ups, Team, and Weekly trend tiles
patterns.desktop: Today spans 8 with Confirmation at 4; Follow-ups, Team, and Weekly trend at 4 each; the alert spans 12. Grouped sidebar on the left.
patterns.mobile: Today, Confirmation, Follow-ups, Team, Weekly trend, Alert, exactly as in the DOM. The sidebar collapses behind a Menu button and breadcrumbs truncate to the parent link.
patterns.conversion: Each tile's action opens its detail view: View day, Review bookings, Open follow-ups, View roster, View report.

patterns.purpose: Document the tile states and layout rules so every page uses the same honest affordances.
sections: Card states heading and one-line rule
Loading, empty, warning, actionable, selected, error, and static tiles, each captioned with its state name
Spans, gaps, and order diagram built in code
Show mobile order toggle with numbered badges
patterns.desktop: State tiles in rows of 4/4/4 and 8/4. The layout diagram shows span 8/4 and 4/4/4 rows on the 12-column grid.
patterns.mobile: States stack in the listed order. The diagram renders the stacked DOM order with numbered badges.
patterns.conversion: No commercial action. Only the actionable tile looks and behaves like a link.
